props.gloss_en: R' Elazar ben Azarya: a basket -- he tilts it on its side and takes [the pot], lest he take [it and ...]
the Sages: he takes [the pot] and returns [it]
Rav: all agree that if the cavity collapsed, it is forbidden to return [the pot]
one master holds: we are concerned lest the cavity collapse
and the other master holds: we are not concerned
Rav Huna: this daffodil branch -- if he inserted it, pulled it out, and inserted it again, it is permitted
Rav Huna: and if not, it is forbidden
Shmuel: this knife between bricks -- if he inserted it, pulled it out, and inserted it again, it is permitted
Shmuel: and if not, it is forbidden
Mar Zutra (or Rav Ashi): in a hedge of reeds it is fine
the mishna: one who buries turnips and radishes under a vine, if some of its leaves were exposed, need not be concerned for kilayim, sheviit or tithes, and they may be taken on Shabbat

challenges.gloss_en: מתיב רב קטינא תיובתא: הטומן לפת וצנונות תחת הגפן ... וניטלין בשבת -- the buried turnips may be taken on Shabbat with no prior loosening; תיובתא (51a.1)

objections.gloss_en: תנן, וחכמים אומרים נוטל ומחזיר. היכי דמי? אי דלא נתקלקלה הגומא -- שפיר קאמרי רבנן; אלא לאו אף על פי שנתקלקלה הגומא -- the Sages permit returning even when the cavity collapsed, so not all agree

answered_by.gloss_en: לא, לעולם דלא נתקלקלה, והכא בחוששין קמיפלגי -- the case is one where the cavity did not collapse; they disagree whether we are concerned lest it collapse (= p_choshshin_shema_nitkalkela / p_ein_choshshin_shema_nitkalkela)
